newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Derivatives disclosure continues to improve - BIS.
newsitem.headline: Derivatives disclosure continues to improve - BIS.

text.p: International banks and securities firms continued to improve their disclosure of trading and derivatives activities in 1995 annual reports, banking and securities supervisors said on Wednesday.

However, there are still disparities in the level of disclosure within, and across countries, with regard to the type and usefulness of information, the Basle Committee on Banking Supervision said following an industry survey.

Regulators, however, are reluctant to impose reporting standards for derivatives because firms are moving in the right direction and any standards now could discourage the evolution toward better practices, supervisors said.
Instead of imposing rules, supervisors prefer to rely on market discipline to push firms to improve disclosure practices.

Information about trading and derivatives activites -- mainly conducted off-balance sheet -- is critical because it allows market participants to gauge the true exposure and financial health of firms.

Transactions with derivatives -- complex financial instruments that are based on underlying securities in cash markets -- have exploded in recent years, but accounting and disclosure methods have in many cases not kept pace.
The collapse of British bank Barings, for example, illustrated the lack of understanding among its top management of the complexity and danger posed by such instruments.
The survey of 1995 annual reports updates a similar survey conducted last year based on the 1994 annual reports of 67 banks and 12 securities firms.

The survey was conducted by the Basle Committee, which groups banking supervisors from the Group of 10 (G10) nations, and the International Organisation of Securities Commissions (IOSCO), which comprises securities supervisors worldwide.
The purpose of the surveys are to review the disclosure practices in the financial industry and stimulate further improvement.

"The Basle Committee and the IOSCO Technical Committee will continue to monitor and to encourage banks and securities firms to improve their disclosure practices further over the coming years," the Basle Committee said in a statement from its secretariat at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
The full report can be accessed from BIS' web site on the Internet at http://www.bis.org.
